insight: Austria's performance in the 2026 FIFA World Cup shows that hydration breaks have a significant impact on their gameplay, with the team gaining momentum in half of the breaks they've taken. When Austria was pressing before a break, they tended to lose momentum, with their average change in momentum being -0.160 per minute, and they were only able to maintain their momentum once out of the five times they were pressing. In contrast, when they weren't pressing before a break, they actually gained momentum, with an average change of +0.100 per minute, suggesting that the breaks gave them a chance to regroup and refocus. Overall, these statistics suggest that Austria benefits from taking breaks when they're not pressing, as it allows them to recharge and come back stronger, while breaks during intense pressing periods can disrupt their rhythm.
